title: Sort Colors
problem_statement:
Given an array nums with n objects colored red, white, or blue (represented by 0, 1, and 2), sort them in-place so that objects of the same color are adjacent, with the colors in the order red, white, and blue.

Input:
First line: N
Second line: N space-separated integers (0, 1, or 2)

Output:
Space-separated sorted integers
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N integers
explanation: Use Dutch National Flag algorithm with three pointers: low, mid, high.

title: Subarray Sums Divisible by K
problem_statement:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the number of non-empty subarrays that have a sum divisible by k.

Input:
Line 1: N K
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Count of subarrays divisible by k
input_format:
Line 1: N K
Line 2: N space-separated integers
explanation: Maintain prefix sum modulo k counts using a hash table.

title: Gas Station
problem_statement:
There are n gas stations along a circular route. You are given two integer arrays gas and cost where gas[i] is the gas at station i and cost[i] is the gas required to travel to station i+1. Return the starting station's index if you can travel around the circuit once clockwise, otherwise return -1.

Input:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N gas values
Line 3: N cost values

Output:
Starting gas station index (0-indexed) or -1
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers
Line 3: N space-separated integers
explanation: If total_gas < total_cost, impossible. Otherwise greedily reset start whenever current tank drops below 0.

title: Find All Duplicates in an Array
problem_statement:
Given an integer array nums of length n where all the integers of nums are in the range [1, n] and each integer appears at most twice, return an array of all the integers that appears twice in ascending order.

Input:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Space-separated integers appearing twice in ascending order, or empty line if none.
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers
explanation: Use sign marking in-place or count frequencies and sort duplicates.

title: Reverse Words in a String
problem_statement:
Given an input string s, reverse the order of the words. A word is defined as a sequence of non-space characters. Return a string of the words in reverse order concatenated by a single space, with leading and trailing spaces removed.

Input:
Single line of text

Output:
Reversed words string
input_format: Single line string
explanation: Split into words by whitespace, reverse word list, and join with space.

title: Longest Repeating Character Replacement
problem_statement:
You are given a string s consisting of only uppercase English letters and an integer k. You can choose any character of the string and change it to any other uppercase letter up to k times. Return the length of the longest substring containing the same letter you can get after performing above operations.

Input:
Line 1: string s
Line 2: integer k

Output:
Maximum length integer
input_format:
Line 1: string
Line 2: integer

examples.explanation: Replace two characters to get AAAA.

explanation: Sliding window where window_length - max_freq <= k.

title: Is Subsequence
problem_statement:
Given two strings s and t, return true if s is a subsequence of t, or false otherwise.

Input:
Line 1: string s
Line 2: string t

Output:
true or false
input_format:
Line 1: string s
Line 2: string t

examples.explanation: abc is a subsequence of ahbgdc.

explanation: Use two pointers, advancing the s pointer only on matching character.

title: Add Binary
problem_statement:
Given two binary strings a and b, return their sum as a binary string.

Input:
Line 1: binary string a
Line 2: binary string b

Output:
Binary sum string
input_format:
Line 1: binary string a
Line 2: binary string b
explanation: Simulate bit-by-bit addition with carry from right to left.

title: Multiply Strings
problem_statement:
Given two non-negative integers num1 and num2 represented as strings, return the product of num1 and num2, also represented as a string without using built-in BigInteger libraries or directly converting inputs to integer.

Input:
Line 1: string num1
Line 2: string num2

Output:
Product string
input_format:
Line 1: num1
Line 2: num2
explanation: Simulate elementary school multiplication storing digit products at indices i+j and i+j+1.

title: Basic Calculator II
problem_statement:
Given a string s which represents an expression with non-negative integers and operators (+, -, *, /), evaluate this expression and return its integer value using integer truncation toward zero.

Input:
Single line string s

Output:
Calculated integer value
input_format: Single line string
explanation: Use a stack to process multiplication and division immediately while deferring addition and subtraction.

title: Next Greater Element I
problem_statement:
The next greater element of some element x in an array is the first greater element that is to the right of x in the same array. Given two distinct 0-indexed integer arrays nums1 and nums2, where nums1 is a subset of nums2, find the next greater element for each value in nums1 in nums2. If no next greater element exists, output -1 for that element.

Input:
Line 1: N1 space-separated integers for nums1
Line 2: N2 space-separated integers for nums2

Output:
Space-separated next greater elements
input_format:
Line 1: nums1
Line 2: nums2

examples.explanation: Next greater for 4 is -1, 1 is 3, 2 is -1.

explanation: Monotonic decreasing stack over nums2 to build next-greater map.

title: Asteroid Collision
problem_statement:
We are given an array asteroids of integers representing asteroids in a row. For each asteroid, the absolute value represents its size, and the sign represents its direction (positive meaning right, negative meaning left). Find out the state of the asteroids after all collisions.

Input:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Space-separated remaining asteroids, or empty line if all explode.
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers
explanation: Use a stack. Collisions only happen when current is negative and stack top is positive.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
problem_statement:
You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. You can only see the k numbers in the window. Return the max sliding window.

Input:
Line 1: N K
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Space-separated max values for each window position
input_format:
Line 1: N K
Line 2: N space-separated integers
explanation: Monotonic decreasing deque holding indices.

title: Largest Rectangle in Histogram
problem_statement:
Given an array of integers heights representing the histogram's bar height where the width of each bar is 1, return the area of the largest rectangle in the histogram.

Input:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Single integer representing maximum area
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers

examples.explanation: The largest rectangle has height 5 and width 2.

explanation: Monotonic increasing stack holding bar indices to compute maximum area in O(N).

title: Merge Two Sorted Lists
problem_statement:
You are given the heads of two sorted linked lists list1 and list2. Merge the two lists into one sorted list and return the space-separated values of the merged list.

Input:
Line 1: space-separated integers of list1
Line 2: space-separated integers of list2

Output:
Space-separated merged sorted integers
input_format:
Line 1: list1 integers
Line 2: list2 integers
explanation: Iterate both lists and append smaller element to output.

title: Add Two Numbers
problem_statement:
You are given two non-empty linked lists representing two non-negative integers. The digits are stored in reverse order, and each of their nodes contains a single digit. Add the two numbers and return the sum as a linked list (in reverse order).

Input:
Line 1: space-separated digits of l1
Line 2: space-separated digits of l2

Output:
Space-separated digits of result list in reverse order
input_format:
Line 1: space-separated digits
Line 2: space-separated digits
explanation: Iterate nodes adding values along with carry from previous addition.

title: Reorder List
problem_statement:
You are given the head of a singly linked-list: L0 -> L1 -> … -> Ln - 1 -> Ln. Reorder the list to be on the following form: L0 -> Ln -> L1 -> Ln - 1 -> L2 -> Ln - 2 -> …

Input:
Space-separated integers of linked list

Output:
Space-separated integers of reordered list
input_format: Single line of integers
explanation: Find middle of list, reverse second half, merge first half and reversed second half alternately.

title: Odd Even Linked List
problem_statement:
Given the head of a singly linked list, group all the nodes with odd indices together followed by the nodes with even indices, and return the reordered list.

Input:
Space-separated integers of list

Output:
Space-separated integers reordered with odd indices then even indices
input_format: Single line of integers
explanation: Maintain odd and even pointers, connect odd.next to even_head at the end.

title: Same Tree
problem_statement:
Given the roots of two binary trees p and q (given as level-order arrays where 'null' indicates empty child), return true if they are structurally identical and nodes have same values, or false otherwise.

Input:
Line 1: level-order traversal of p
Line 2: level-order traversal of q

Output:
true or false
input_format:
Line 1: space-separated values for p
Line 2: space-separated values for q
explanation: Recursively check if p.val == q.val and sameTree(p.left, q.left) and sameTree(p.right, q.right).

title: Diameter of Binary Tree
problem_statement:
Given the root of a binary tree (as a level-order array), return the length of the diameter of the tree. The diameter is the length of the longest path between any two nodes in a tree, measured by number of edges.

Input:
Level-order values separated by spaces

Output:
Single integer representing diameter
input_format: Single line string of tree nodes

examples.explanation: Longest path is [4,2,1,3] or [5,2,1,3] of length 3.

explanation: DFS returning height and updating max_diameter = max(max_diameter, left_height + right_height).

title: Binary Tree Right Side View
problem_statement:
Given the root of a binary tree, imagine yourself standing on the right side of it, return the values of the nodes you can see ordered from top to bottom.

Input:
Level-order traversal of binary tree

Output:
Space-separated values visible from right side
input_format: Single line of tree nodes
explanation: BFS level-order traversal taking the last element of each level queue.

title: Kth Smallest Element in a BST
problem_statement:
Given the root of a binary search tree and an integer k, return the kth smallest value (1-indexed) of all the values of the nodes in the tree.

Input:
Line 1: Level-order BST nodes
Line 2: Integer k

Output:
kth smallest integer value
input_format:
Line 1: BST nodes
Line 2: k
explanation: In-order traversal yields sorted order. Stop at kth visited node.

title: Flatten Binary Tree to Linked List
problem_statement:
Given the root of a binary tree, flatten the tree into a pre-order 'linked list' where right child pointer points to the next node and left child pointer is always null.

Input:
Level-order traversal of tree

Output:
Pre-order flattened sequence separated by spaces
input_format: Single line of nodes
explanation: Pre-order traversal linking nodes to the right.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
problem_statement:
A path in a binary tree is a sequence of nodes where each pair of adjacent nodes has an edge connecting them. A node can only appear in the sequence at most once. Return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path.

Input:
Level-order traversal of tree nodes

Output:
Maximum path sum integer
input_format: Single line of tree nodes
explanation: Post-order DFS computing max gain from left and right children, updating global maximum sum.

title: Rotting Oranges
problem_statement:
You are given an m x n grid where each cell can have one of three values: 0 representing empty cell, 1 representing fresh orange, or 2 representing rotten orange. Every minute, any fresh orange that is 4-directionally adjacent to a rotten orange becomes rotten. Return the minimum number of minutes that must elapse until no cell has a fresh orange. If impossible, return -1.

Input:
Line 1: M N
Next M lines: N space-separated integers

Output:
Minimum minutes or -1
input_format:
Line 1: M N
Followed by M lines of grid

examples.explanation: Takes 4 minutes to rot all fresh oranges.

explanation: Multi-source BFS initialized with all initially rotten oranges.

title: Surrounded Regions
problem_statement:
Given an m x n matrix board containing 'X' and 'O', capture all regions that are 4-directionally surrounded by 'X'. A region is captured by flipping all 'O's into 'X's in that surrounded region.

Input:
Line 1: M N
Next M lines: N characters ('X' or 'O') separated by spaces

Output:
M lines: N space-separated characters representing the board after capture
input_format:
Line 1: M N
M lines of matrix

examples.input:
4 4
X X X X
X O O X
X X O X
X O X X
examples.output:
X X X X
X X X X
X X X X
X O X X
examples.explanation: Surrounded O regions flipped to X.

explanation: DFS/BFS from boundary 'O's marking un-capturable cells, then flip all remaining 'O's to 'X'.

test_cases.input:
4 4
X X X X
X O O X
X X O X
X O X X
test_cases.expected_output:
X X X X
X X X X
X X X X
X O X X

test_cases.input:
3 3
X X X
X O X
X X X
test_cases.expected_output:
X X X
X X X
X X X

title: Word Search
problem_statement:
Given an m x n grid of characters board and a string word, return true if word exists in the grid. The word can be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, where adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring. The same letter cell may not be used more than once.

Input:
Line 1: M N
Next M lines: N characters separated by space
Last line: target word

Output:
true or false
input_format:
Line 1: M N
M lines of board
Line M+2: word

examples.input:
3 4
A B C E
S F C S
A D E E
ABCCED

explanation: Backtracking with DFS from each cell matching the first character of word.

test_cases.input:
3 4
A B C E
S F C S
A D E E
ABCCED

3 4
A B C E
S F C S
A D E E
SEE

3 4
A B C E
S F C S
A D E E
ABCB

title: Unique Paths
problem_statement:
There is a robot on an m x n grid. The robot is initially located at the top-left corner (i.e., grid[0][0]). The robot tries to move to the bottom-right corner (i.e., grid[m - 1][n - 1]). The robot can only move either down or right at any point in time. Given the two integers m and n, return the number of possible unique paths.

Input:
Two integers m and n separated by space

Output:
Number of unique paths integer
input_format: m n
explanation: Combinations C(m+n-2, m-1) or 2D DP dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j] + dp[i][j-1].

title: Minimum Path Sum
problem_statement:
Given a m x n grid filled with non-negative numbers, find a path from top left to bottom right, which minimizes the sum of all numbers along its path. You can only move either down or right at any point in time.

Input:
Line 1: M N
Next M lines: N space-separated integers

Output:
Minimum path sum
input_format:
Line 1: M N
M lines of grid values
explanation: dp[i][j] = grid[i][j] + min(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

title: Longest Common Subsequence
problem_statement:
Given two strings text1 and text2, return the length of their longest common subsequence. If there is no common subsequence, return 0.

Input:
Line 1: string text1
Line 2: string text2

Output:
Length of LCS
input_format:
Line 1: text1
Line 2: text2
explanation: 2D DP: dp[i][j] = dp[i-1][j-1] + 1 if match else max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

title: House Robber II
problem_statement:
You are a professional robber planning to rob houses along a street. Each house has a certain amount of money stashed. All houses at this place are arranged in a circle. That means the first house is the neighbor of the last one. Adjacent houses have security systems connected and it will automatically contact the police if two adjacent houses were broken into on the same night. Return the maximum amount of money you can rob tonight without alerting the police.

Input:
Space-separated integers of house values

Output:
Maximum rob amount
input_format: Single line of integers

examples.explanation: Cannot rob house 1 and 3 because they are adjacent in circle.

explanation: Compute max(rob(nums[1:]), rob(nums[:-1])) using linear house robber logic.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
problem_statement:
Given an integer array nums, return true if you can partition the array into two subsets such that the sum of the elements in both subsets is equal or false otherwise.

Input:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
true or false
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers
explanation: 0/1 Knapsack: check if subset with sum equal to total_sum // 2 exists when total_sum is even.

title: Target Sum
problem_statement:
You are given an integer array nums and an integer target. You want to build an expression out of nums by adding one of the symbols '+' and '-' before each integer in nums and then concatenate all the integers. Return the number of different expressions that you can build, which evaluate to target.

Input:
Line 1: N target
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Number of ways integer
input_format:
Line 1: N target
Line 2: N integers

examples.explanation: 5 ways to assign signs to evaluate to 3.

explanation: Subset sum formulation: positive_subset = (target + total_sum) // 2.

title: Non-overlapping Intervals
problem_statement:
Given an array of intervals intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi], return the minimum number of intervals you need to remove to make the rest of the intervals non-overlapping.

Input:
Line 1: N
Next N lines: start and end of each interval

Output:
Minimum removed intervals integer
input_format:
Line 1: N
N lines of intervals
explanation: Sort by end time greedily keeping intervals that finish earliest.

title: Minimum Number of Arrows to Burst Balloons
problem_statement:
There are spherical balloons taped to a flat wall represented by intervals points where points[i] = [xstart, xend]. An arrow shot vertically upwards from x bursts all balloons whose horizontal extent contains x. Return the minimum number of arrows that must be shot to burst all balloons.

Input:
Line 1: N
Next N lines: xstart and xend of each balloon

Output:
Minimum arrows integer
input_format:
Line 1: N
N lines of intervals

examples.explanation: Shoot at x=6 (bursts [2,8] and [1,6]) and x=11 (bursts [10,16] and [7,12]).

explanation: Sort by end coordinate. Shoot arrow at end of earliest ending balloon.

title: Insert Interval
problem_statement:
You are given an array of non-overlapping intervals intervals where intervals[i] = [starti, endi] sorted in ascending order by starti. You are also given an interval newInterval = [start, end]. Insert newInterval into intervals such that intervals is still sorted in ascending order by starti and intervals still does not have any overlapping intervals (merge overlapping intervals if necessary).

Input:
Line 1: N
Next N lines: existing intervals
Last line: newInterval start and end

Output:
M lines: merged non-overlapping intervals
input_format:
Line 1: N
N lines: intervals
Last line: newInterval
explanation: Add intervals before newInterval, merge all overlapping, add intervals after.

title: Number of 1 Bits
problem_statement:
Write a function that takes the binary representation of a positive integer and returns the number of set bits ('1's) it has (also known as the Hamming weight).

Input:
Single integer n

Output:
Count of set bits
input_format: Single integer

examples.explanation: 11 in binary is 1011 which has three set bits.

explanation: Brian Kernighan's algorithm: n &= (n - 1) repeatedly clears the lowest set bit.

title: Counting Bits
problem_statement:
Given an integer n, return an array ans of length n + 1 such that for each i (0 <= i <= n), ans[i] is the number of 1's in the binary representation of i.

Input:
Single integer n

Output:
Space-separated counts of 1s from 0 to n
input_format: Single integer

title: Reverse Bits
problem_statement:
Reverse bits of a given 32 bits unsigned integer.

Input:
Single integer n

Output:
Integer with reversed 32-bit binary representation
input_format: Single integer
explanation: Iterate 32 times: res = (res << 1) | (n & 1); n >>= 1.

title: Single Number II
problem_statement:
Given an integer array nums where every element appears three times except for one, which appears exactly once. Find the single element and return it.

Input:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Single unique integer
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers
explanation: Sum bits mod 3 for each bit position 0..31 or use twos and ones bitmask transitions.

title: Happy Number
problem_statement:
Write an algorithm to determine if a number n is happy. A happy number is a number defined by the following process: Starting with any positive integer, replace the number by the sum of the squares of its digits. Repeat the process until the number equals 1 (where it will stay), or it loops endlessly in a cycle which does not include 1.

Input:
Single integer n

Output:
true or false
input_format: Single integer
explanation: Floyd's cycle-finding algorithm or hash set of visited numbers.

title: Sqrt(x)
problem_statement:
Given a non-negative integer x, return the square root of x rounded down to the nearest integer. The returned integer should be non-negative as well.

Input:
Single integer x

Output:
Integer square root
input_format: Single integer
explanation: Binary search between 0 and x.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring
problem_statement:
Given a string s, return the longest palindromic substring in s.

Input:
Single line string s

Output:
Longest palindromic substring
input_format: Single line string

examples.explanation: 'bab' is a valid longest palindrome ('aba' also acceptable).

explanation: Expand around centers at each index i and between i and i+1.

title: Decode String
problem_statement:
Given an encoded string, return its decoded string. The encoding rule is: k[encoded_string], where the encoded_string inside the square brackets is being repeated exactly k times. Note that k is guaranteed to be a positive integer.

Input:
Single line encoded string

Output:
Decoded string
input_format: Single line string
explanation: Use a stack to keep track of current multiplier count and previous string segments.

title: Find Peak Element
problem_statement:
A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors. Given a 0-indexed integer array nums, find a peak element, and return its index. If the array contains multiple peaks, return the index to any of the peaks.

Input:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers

Output:
Index of any peak element
input_format:
Line 1: N
Line 2: N space-separated integers
explanation: Binary search: if nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], peak must lie in right half.
